summary: iter23 backend testing PASSED 17/17. Banking statements draft/posted workflow fully verified. POST /statements creates with status='draft'. GET returns computed_closing/balance_diff/is_balanced correctly. Credit/debit signs (credit=+, debit=-) handled on mixed txns. POST /{id}/post refuses 400 when unbalanced (error message contains opening, mvts, closing, diff), succeeds 200 when balanced (sets posted_at). Re-posting already-posted returns 400. /unpost reverts to draft. PUT updates number/date/account_number/opening/closing. Rounding tolerance 0.01 verified (diff<0.01 -> balanced, diff>=0.01 -> not). Regression iter22 cascade DELETE, iter21 IBAN->PCMN resolution and iter20 balance owners all PASS.

minor.issue: Pre-existing data drift in ACP demo: Alex BENOIT balance is now 614.60 (was 314.60). Likely from accumulated test residue or seed changes. Affects iter22 absolute-value assertions only; the endpoint logic is correct. Not iter23-related.
Does not check if statement is currently 'posted' before unposting; will silently set draft on an already-draft statement. Minor UX/correctness.

No status guard: a 'posted' statement can be modified (opening/closing/account) via PUT. Should probably refuse 400 if status='posted' (or require unpost first), otherwise balance integrity of posted statements can drift.
Does not validate that statement has at least 1 transaction. An empty statement with opening==closing posts successfully (may be intended).

action_items: Consider blocking PUT/DELETE on statements with status='posted' (require unpost first) to preserve integrity.
Consider blocking /unpost when status is already 'draft' (return 400 with clear message).
Re-baseline iter22 hardcoded balance expectation (Alex BENOIT 614.60 vs 314.60) or re-seed demo ACP.
critical_code_review_comments: banking.py update_statement (line 176-188): no status guard - posted statements can be edited and silently break balance integrity. Recommend: if stmt['status']=='posted' raise 400.
banking.py unpost_statement (line 165-174): does not check current status; should return 400 if status is already 'draft' instead of silently overwriting.

banking.py post_statement: balance check uses sum() with float arithmetic - using Decimal would be more robust for accounting; current round(,2) + 0.01 tolerance is acceptable but document the tolerance.

banking.py StatementInput (line 9-15): PUT /statements/{id} reuses StatementInput which requires 'number' and 'date' as mandatory - partial updates not supported. Consider StatementUpdateInput with all optional fields.

banking.py: 'status' field missing from StatementInput - cannot be set on POST (acceptable since default='draft'), but no API exists to manually set to posted bypassing balance check (correct by design).
banking.py list_statements: response does NOT include computed_closing/is_balanced fields (only GET by id does). Frontend listing cannot show balance state without N+1 GETs.
banking.py file is 528 lines - still well within the 700-line threshold, no split needed yet.
